name: Singapore
tagline: The Garden City Where Hawker Food Is Paradise and All of Asia Is Your Backyard — Retire in Singapore
description: Singapore is a paradox for FIRE retirees: housing and car ownership are among the world's most expensive, yet you can eat an award-winning plate of chicken rice for $3 at a hawker center. This ultra-modern city-state combines tropical garden beauty, world-class healthcare, absolute safety, and seamless efficiency. As Asia's premier hub, weekend flights to Bali, Bangkok, and Tokyo are cheap and plentiful. English is widely spoken, the rule of law is ironclad, and the food — from Michelin-starred hawker stalls to cutting-edge fine dining — is legendary.

quickFacts.visa: 90-day tourist visa on arrival for US citizens. No dedicated retirement visa. Global Investor Programme requires S$10M+ investment. Most retirees cycle 90-day tourist entries or base in nearby Malaysia (MM2H program).
quickFacts.language: English, Mandarin, Malay, Tamil (English is the primary business and government language)
quickFacts.internetSpeed: 300–1000 Mbps (among the fastest and most reliable in the world)
quickFacts.safetyRating: Extremely Safe — consistently ranked among the safest cities globally; near-zero violent crime
quickFacts.nearestAirport: Singapore Changi (SIN) — consistently voted world's best airport; gateway to all of Asia and Oceania
quickFacts.climate: Equatorial tropical with consistent heat and humidity year-round; frequent afternoon thunderstorms; no distinct seasons

housing.description: Modest whole studio or small 1-bedroom — a rented studio condo or whole HDB unit in an outlying area (Woodlands, Jurong, Tampines)

dining.description: Hawker centre meals daily — chicken rice, laksa, char kway teow — genuinely excellent at S$4–6 a plate

healthcare.description: Individual private/international plan (~50yo); non-PR residents cannot use MediShield, so private cover is required

transportation.description: MRT and bus on an EZ-Link card — no car needed

entertainment.description: Gardens by the Bay, East Coast Park cycling, free events, hawker socialising

1M.lifestyle: A modest whole studio or small 1-bedroom — a rented studio condo or a whole HDB unit in an outlying area like Woodlands, Jurong, or Tampines — because renting a private space here means real money even at the bottom. Daily eating leans on the hawker centres, where a plate of chicken rice or laksa is genuinely excellent for a few dollars, and the spotless MRT covers the island with no car needed. Private health cover is required, since non-PR residents cannot tap MediShield. This is a disciplined budget for Singapore — housing and insurance are the squeeze — but the safety, transit, and food quality are hard to match anywhere on Earth.

housing.description: Comfortable 1-bedroom or small 2-bedroom HDB flat or entry-level condo in areas like Toa Payoh, Queenstown, or Tiong Bahru

dining.description: Mix of hawker centers, coffee shops, and mid-range restaurants — omakase at neighborhood sushi bars, seafood at East Coast, and weekend dim sum

healthcare.description: Comprehensive private insurance (Integrated Shield Plan upgrade); access to excellent private hospitals like Mount Elizabeth and Gleneagles

transportation.description: MRT and bus daily, supplemented by Grab rides; no need for a car — Singapore is designed to be car-free

entertainment.description: Swimming, gym membership, weekend trips to Sentosa, cinema, museum visits, and budget flights to regional destinations

2M.lifestyle: A comfortable 1-bedroom condo or whole HDB flat in a mid neighbourhood like Toa Payoh or Queenstown, mixing hawker centres with neighbourhood restaurants and weekend dim sum. MRT and bus daily with Grab on top, comprehensive private cover, and cheap regional flights. Efficient and comfortable, though middle-class by Singapore standards. (Interpolated tier.)

housing.description: Proper 1-bedroom condo with pool and gym in a desirable district (River Valley, Holland Village, Bukit Timah)

dining.description: Good restaurants several times a week between beloved hawker meals

healthcare.description: Comprehensive private/international insurance; Mount Elizabeth and Gleneagles access

entertainment.description: Symphony, premium gym, diving trips, frequent regional travel

3M.lifestyle: A proper 1-bedroom condo with pool and gym in a desirable district like River Valley, Holland Village, or Bukit Timah, with dining at good restaurants several times a week between beloved hawker meals. MRT plus regular Grab covers mobility, and comprehensive private insurance brings access to Mount Elizabeth and Gleneagles. Cheap weekend flights reach Bali, Bangkok, or Tokyo. This is Singapore's sweet spot — genuinely comfortable — though the city's costs mean it does not feel lavish.

housing.description: Luxury condo or landed property in prime District 9, 10, or 11 — Orchard, Tanglin, or a black-and-white colonial bungalow in Dempsey

dining.description: Standing reservations at Odette, Burnt Ends, and Les Amis; private dining experiences; imported Japanese wagyu and French wine pairings

healthcare.description: VIP healthcare with concierge services at Mount Elizabeth; annual comprehensive screenings; international medical evacuation coverage

transportation.description: Hired car with driver (owning a car in Singapore costs $100K+ in COE alone); business class flights around Asia

entertainment.description: Singapore Island Country Club membership, yacht charters to Indonesian islands, Formula 1 Grand Prix paddock access, and luxury resort weekends across the region

domesticHelp.description: Live-in foreign domestic worker (common and well-regulated in Singapore), plus weekly professional cleaning service

luxuryExtras.description: Bespoke tailoring on Savile Row visits, premium whisky and wine collection, luxury island resort weekends, and art acquisitions at Singapore Art Week

5M.lifestyle: A luxury 1-bedroom or compact 2-bedroom in a prime district — Orchard, Tanglin, or River Valley — with a live-in helper and weekly cleaning, a hired car with driver, and standing reservations at the city's top tables. VIP healthcare at Mount Elizabeth, business-class regional flights, and yacht charters to the Indonesian islands. High quality and genuinely comfortable, though even here Singapore's costs require some choices. (Interpolated tier.)

housing.description: Prime-district luxury condo at Marina Bay or Orchard with skyline views

dining.description: Fine dining as routine plus a private chef a few days a week

healthcare.description: Top-tier international/concierge cover with 24/7 specialist access

transportation.description: On-demand chauffeured car (owning a car runs six figures in COE) plus first-class flights

entertainment.description: Elite club memberships, superyacht access, private art viewings, luxury travel

domesticHelp.description: A live-in helper plus a part-time cook for the residence

luxuryExtras.description: Rare-wine vault, bespoke global travel, contemporary-art acquisitions

10M.lifestyle: A prime-district luxury condo at Marina Bay or Orchard with skyline views, a live-in helper and a part-time cook for the residence, and an on-demand chauffeured car (owning a car here runs six figures in COE alone). Top-tier international health cover with 24/7 specialist access, fine dining as routine, and elite club and yacht memberships. Singapore's extreme housing and healthcare floors absorb a real share even at this level, so life is frictionless and upper-affluent rather than limitless by local standards — and still, by a wide margin, the most expensive address in the region.
